title: Guruvāyūr
body:
Mūlavar: Guruvāyūrappan
Pushkariṇī: Nārāyaṇa Saras
Location: the town of Guruvāyūr, in Kerala

The Vow of Pṛśni

According to tradition, Lord Guruvāyūrappan's story begins even before the dawn of the Kṛta Yuga. There was once a couple, Pṛśni and Sutapas, who longed for children. To be blessed with them, Pṛśni undertook a vratam of twelve days, in which she offered milk to the Lord and took nothing but that milk herself. Having taken it, she would sit in meditation upon the Lord, chanting the mantram "Om Namo Bhagavate Vāsudevāya."

On the thirteenth day, Lord Mahāvishṇu appeared before Pṛśni, bearing the śankham, chakram, gadā and padmam. Seeing the Lord before her, Pṛśni was struck speechless. The Lord touched His conch, the Pāñcajanya, to her cheek and then to her throat, and the first words that came from her lips were "Sriman Nārāyaṇa." The Lord told her that she could speak again, and asked her to seek the children she desired.

Gazing upon the Lord's beauty, she asked that He Himself become her child. So overwhelmed was she by His form that she asked it three times, and before she could open her lips a fourth time, the Lord gently closed her mouth. He told Pṛśni that her request had placed Him in a difficult position: because she had asked Him three times, and had performed her vratam with the utmost bhakti, He was now bound to be born to her three times.

Pṛśni then asked the Lord not to give her children, but simply to remain with her as He had appeared. The Lord told her that He could not remain in bodily form. Instead, He would fashion a vigraham bearing all His features, a foot and a half tall. She was to regard it as the Lord Himself, keep it safe, and perform the daily pūjā to it. He would be born three times, He said, with Pṛśni as His mother and Sutapas as His father, and in each of those births He too would worship the vigraham.

In the first birth, the Lord was born to Pṛśni and Sutapas as Pṛśnigarbhan. In the second, Pṛśni and Sutapas were reborn as Aditi and Kaśyapa, and the Lord was born to them as Vāmana. In the third, they were reborn as Dēvaki and Vasudēva, and the Lord was born to them as Sri Kṛshṇa. After His birth to Dēvaki, the Lord reminded them of their earlier lives and told them that His debt to them was now fulfilled.

From Dvārakā to Guru and Vāyu

At the close of the Dvāpara Yuga, before He ascended to Paramapadam, Sri Kṛshṇa entrusted the vigraham to Uddhava, wishing it to be preserved for the ages to come. The vigraham is said to be made of a stone called Pātāla Anjanam, found only in Sri Vaikuṇṭham. Sri Kṛshṇa explained to Uddhava that the coming age would be the Kali Yuga, filled with adharmam. In such a time, He wished that there should be a presence that would answer the prayers of His devotees and protect them from every danger. So He gave the vigraham to Uddhava and asked him to keep it safe, and to build a temple for it after the pralayam.

Soon Sri Kṛshṇa ascended to Paramapadam, and the pralayam swept over the world. As the great flood was about to engulf Uddhava, he raised his eyes to the sky and saw Bṛhaspati, the Guru of the Dēvas, and Vāyu Dēva. He called them at once and entrusted the vigraham to them, together with the duty of establishing a temple for the Lord.

In the first age the Lord had been worshipped as Nārāyaṇa, in the second as Keśava, in the third as Mādhava, and in the Kali Yuga He is worshipped as Sri Kṛshṇa. Thus Āṇḍāḷ begins her Tiruppāvai with "Nārāyaṇanē namakkē paṛai tharuvān," and ends it with "Vangak kaḍal kaḍaindha Mādhavanai, Kēsavanai."

Uddhava asked Guru and Vāyu to hold the Lord in their care until the Kali Yuga reached a time when mountains had risen, rivers flowed, the oceans raged, and men built houses; and then to wait until they found a person who they believed would worship the Lord with reverence. When they found such a person, they were to hand the vigraham to him and establish a temple for the Lord.

Guru and Vāyu held the Lord in their hands, served Him in kainkaryam, and waited for the time when all of Uddhava's conditions would be fulfilled.

The Land at Mammiyūr

At last Guru and Vāyu came to the skies above the earth and began searching for a place where they might entrust the Lord to humankind. As they passed over Kerala, they heard a voice calling to them, asking them to hand the Lord over. Looking down, they saw Lord Śiva and Pārvatī Dēvī, who offered them land on which to install the Lord.

Even today, near Guruvāyūr, stands the Śiva kshethram of Mammiyūr, about a kilometre and a half away. Lord Śiva and Pārvatī Dēvī, having given land for the Lord at that distance from their own shrine, wished that they too might have the privilege of housing the Lord in their temple. It is said that the Lord fashioned another vigraham of Himself in Sri Vaikuṇṭham, a little taller, and placed it in their care. To this day, a visitor to Mammiyūr can see a taller vigraham of Guruvāyūrappan beside the sanctum of Lord Śiva and Pārvatī Dēvī.

Nārāyaṇa Saras

Guru and Vāyu placed the vigraham a kilometre and a half from Mammiyūr and resolved to build a temple there. As soon as the Lord heard of their decision, the vigraham spoke. Before they built the temple, He said, He wished for a tank to be made, not set apart or tucked away in a corner, but forming part of the temple itself, so that devotees could bathe in it and enter the temple at once.

As the Lord instructed, Guru summoned Varuṇa Dēva, and the tank was built. As soon as it was ready, the Lord said that He wished to bathe in it. Guru and Vāyu placed Him upon a plate of solid gold and bathed Him in its waters, and the Lord named the tank Nārāyaṇa Saras.

Then Dēvaguru Bṛhaspati summoned all the Dēvas and performed the Ashṭabandhana Samprōkshaṇa Kumbhābhishēkam, establishing the temple and completing the consecration of the Lord.

The Lord was pleased with Guru and Vāyu and asked them to stand before Him. He told all the Dēvas that, in an age when humankind would scarcely spare a thought for the Lord, Guru and Vāyu had kept their promise to Uddhava with immense devotion and established a temple for Him. In their honour, the Lord named the kshethram Guruvāyūr, and since He stands there, He asked to be known as Guruvāyūrappan.

Approaching the Lord

As one enters the temple, one should remember the Lord and call out to Him as Nārāyaṇa. Passing the maṇḍapam where Sri Nārāyaṇa Bhaṭṭatiri composed the Nārāyaṇīyam, one should remember Him and call out to Him as Kṛshṇa. And finally, approaching the sanctum, one should remember Him and call out to Him as Guruvāyūrappan:

"O Nārāyaṇa, Kṛshṇa, Guruvāyūrappa, protect me and be my refuge."
